item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and far more reviewable, though it still incorrectly changes Add and bypasses it from Upload.","reasons":["A adds the exact Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and verifies filename, content, multipart encoding, and retry replay from an os.File.","B explicitly adds forbidden association fields and seven new typed options plus WithFileFormValues, changing FilesOption behavior beyond the contract.","B expands scope into global Raw.Do/request-body ownership, seeking, Content-Length, retry behavior, documentation, and multipart helper machinery, all expressly outside the requested change.","Neither Upload routes through the existing Add method: A calls a new private add helper, while B duplicates Add's request construction and response decoding. A's factoring at least keeps those paths sharing one implementation internally; B leaves duplicate machinery that can drift."],"risks_a":["Add no longer preserves existing behavior: it now reads every caller-encoded body fully into memory and may return a read error before issuing the request.","The patch lacks visible Upload tests for empty filename, nil content, and source-reader failures, despite those being required.","The combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors would be."],"risks_b":["Adds association APIs and multipart fields explicitly prohibited by the contract.","Upload uses NewFileWithFields and calls Raw.Do directly instead of reusing NewFile and routing through Add.","Globally changes replay, closing, and Content-Length semantics for Raw.Do, Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, and other callers, creating broad compatibility risk unrelated to the task scope despite preserved gates in the benchmark context. It also lacks a visible source-reader failure test."]}
